sentences.en: The spaces we are in every day influence our mood and well-being, whether we're aware of it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论我们是否意识到，我们每天身处的空间都会影响我们的情绪和幸福感。

sentences.en: Creating spaces to make us feel our best is a hot topic in community planning, in the office, and on HGTV.
sentences.zh: 打造能让我们感觉最佳的空间是社区规划、办公室以及 HGTV 上的热门话题。

sentences.en: Here to talk about designing spaces to optimize well-being is A-P-A fellow, Dr. Sally
sentences.zh: 今天做客节目、跟我们聊聊如何通过设计空间来优化幸福感的是美国心理协会会士、萨莉·奥古斯丁

sentences.en: Augustine, an environmental psychologist who is a principal at Design with Science, a design consultation firm.
sentences.zh: 博士，她是一位环境心理学家，也是设计咨询公司“科学设计”的负责人。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Augustine.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，奥古斯丁博士。

sentences.en: Nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So the start of 2019 brought us the Marie
sentences.zh: 2019 年的开始给我们带来了玛丽

sentences.en: Kondo effect is what I'll be calling it.
sentences.zh: 孔多效应，我暂且这么称呼它。

sentences.en: She's the famous Japanese professional organizer whose show on Netflix called Tidying Up has been wildly popular.
sentences.zh: 她是日本著名的专业收纳师，她在 Netflix 上名叫《整理魔法》的节目大受欢迎。

sentences.en: So Americans seem hungry for this type of program to show us how to declutter our lives and our homes.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国人似乎渴望这类节目来教我们如何清理生活和家里的杂物。

sentences.en: And as a design psychologist, what are your thoughts on the response to the show?
sentences.zh: 作为一名设计心理学家，你对大众对这个节目的反应有什么看法？

sentences.en: I think the response to the show indicates how burdened so many of us are by all the things in our physical environment.
sentences.zh: 我认为，大家对这个节目的反应表明，我们当中有太多人被物理环境中的各种物品压得喘不过气来。

sentences.en: We have books, we have tchotchkes, we have all sorts of stuff that surround us.
sentences.zh: 我们有书本，我们有小摆设，我们身边充斥着各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And all those materials create an environment that's really very complex visually.
sentences.zh: 所有这些材料创造出了一个在视觉上非常复杂的环境。

sentences.en: And when we're in a complicated visual environment, we feel stress.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于一个复杂的视觉环境中时，我们会感到压力。

sentences.en: So I think the success of the Marie Kondo show indicates that people really, really need to tone back all the visual activity in the spaces that are around them.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，玛丽·孔多节目的成功表明，人们真的非常需要减少身边空间中所有的视觉活动。

sentences.en: And they need to create a space that has about the same number of colors, shapes, patterns, etc.
sentences.zh: 他们需要创造这样一个空间：其中的颜色、形状、图案等数量，

sentences.en: as they're likely to find in an interior designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.
sentences.zh: 大概和弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特设计的室内空间差不多。

sentences.en: Can you explain more why clutter makes us stressed?
sentences.zh: 你能多解释一下为什么杂物会让我们感到压力吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like Americans tend to have too much stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国人似乎往往拥有太多东西。

sentences.en: And it makes us stressed.
sentences.zh: 这让我们感到压力。

sentences.en: But giving it away and getting it getting rid of it is difficult.
sentences.zh: 但把它们送人或扔掉却很困难。

sentences.en: So can you talk about why clutter, though, is still stressful for us?
sentences.zh: 所以你能谈谈为什么杂物对我们来说仍然压力重重吗？

sentences.en: Clutter is stressful for us, because whether you realize it or not, you're always surveying the environment around you.
sentences.zh: 杂物之所以让我们感到压力，是因为无论你有没有意识到，你总是在环顾四周的环境。

sentences.en: This is because our mental apparatus evolved millennia ago, and we're still using the same sort of brain systems to assess our world now that we did in the paSt. So
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们的心理机制在几千年前就进化出来了，我们评估世界的大脑系统和过去相比依然没有变。所以

sentences.en: when we were young as a species, it was very important for us to be continually looking around our world, making sure that nothing that found us tasty was approaching.
sentences.zh: 当我们的物种还处于早期阶段时，持续环顾四周、确保没有什么觉得我们美味可口的动物在靠近，对我们来说至关重要。

sentences.en: And when there's more going on around us visually, it's harder to spot tigers, whatever that might be lurking out there.
sentences.zh: 当周围视觉上发生的事情更多时，就更难发现老虎或潜伏在那里的其他什么东西。

sentences.en: So when we're in a space that's more complex visually, we get stressed out.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们处于视觉上更复杂的空间时，我们就会感到压力山大。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really interesting how it goes back so much further than just the current day, how it's a part of our biology.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很有趣，它竟然能追溯到远超现代的时期，这是我们生物学的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is intriguing to think about all the vestiges of our primordial selves, if you will, that continue to be important in our world.
sentences.zh: 是的，一想到我们原始自我的种种痕迹——如果你愿意这么叫的话——在我们的世界中依然重要，就真的很耐人寻味。

sentences.en: And can you talk about your work you do at Design with Science?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊你在“科学设计”所做的工作吗？

sentences.en: How did you get started?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: And what type of clients do you work with?
sentences.zh: 你跟什么样的客户合作？

sentences.en: Well, I have an MBA as well as a PhD.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我既有工商管理硕士学位，也有博士学位。

sentences.en: And I got involved in retail design projects as the sort of management type, if you will, when I graduated from business school and was intrigued by how the
sentences.zh: 我从商学院毕业后，作为管理层类型的人——如果你愿意这么说的话——参与了零售设计项目，并对商店里的

sentences.en: physical environment in stores influenced what people think and behave.
sentences.zh: 物理环境如何影响人们的想法和行为产生了浓厚兴趣。

sentences.en: That led me to go back to school to study environmental psychology and led me to my current practice where I work with people who are designing places or objects or services.
sentences.zh: 这促使我重返校园研究环境心理学，并让我走向了目前的实践，我与那些设计场所、物品或服务的人合作。

sentences.en: And I make recommendations based on environmental psych research that make desired activities, outcomes, et cetera, more likely.
sentences.zh: 我根据环境心理学研究提出建议，使期望的活动、结果等更有可能发生。

sentences.en: So I will make suggestions about what colors walls should be painted in order to enhance creative performance in a space or
sentences.zh: 因此，我会就墙壁应该刷什么颜色提出建议，以便增强空间中的创造性表现，或者

sentences.en: how ceiling heights come into play, how the textures we feel make a difference in our lives.
sentences.zh: 天花板高度如何发挥作用，我们感受到的质感如何在我们的生活中产生影响。

sentences.en: And I work with people all over the world to get environmental psych research out of all sorts of journals and into the world where it can make a difference in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 我与世界各地的人合作，将各种期刊上的环境心理学研究成果应用到现实世界中，从而在人们的生活中发挥作用。

sentences.en: It seems like more businesses and people are interested in designing good spaces today.
sentences.zh: 似乎现在有更多的企业和个人对设计良好的空间感兴趣。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just, has it always been an interest?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这一直都是人们的兴趣所在？

sentences.en: I think at one level, it's always been an interest, you know, since the, you know, first,
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，这一直都是人们的兴趣所在，你知道的，自从第一个

sentences.en: you know, person tried to sell something to some other person that, you know, they've been
sentences.zh: 人试图把某样东西卖给另一个人起，你知道的，他们就一直

sentences.en: motivated to create an environment conducive to that.
sentences.zh: 有动力去创造一个有利于达成目标的 ambientales 环境。

sentences.en: I have seen increased attention to applying environmental psychology in the last few years, because people are becoming more aware that there is a
sentences.zh: 我发现过去几年里，人们对应用环境心理学的关注度有所增加，因为人们越来越意识到，有

sentences.en: science that can be used to design environments and make particular outcomes and situations more likely.
sentences.zh: 一门科学可以用来设计环境，并使特定的结果和情况更有可能发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now I want to get into more of the design details, how they, how they influence us.
sentences.zh: 现在我想探讨更多设计细节，它们是如何影响我们的。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how our emotions are influenced by colors, patterns, lighting, and texture?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈我们的情绪是如何受到颜色、图案、光线和质感影响的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: I'll start with color, because this is what I'm asked about most frequently.
sentences.zh: 我从颜色开始讲起，因为这是我被问到频率最高的问题。

sentences.en: Color has three attributes.
sentences.zh: 颜色有三个属性。

sentences.en: You know, there's hue, which is the name we give to a collection of wavelengths.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有色相，这是我们给一组波长起的名字。

sentences.en: And there's also saturation and brightness.
sentences.zh: 此外还有饱和度和明度。

sentences.en: Saturation is how true a color is.
sentences.zh: 饱和度是指颜色的纯度。

sentences.en: So like a khaki green is less saturated than a kelly green.
sentences.zh: 比如卡其绿的饱和度就比亮绿色低。

sentences.en: You also might think of saturation as how much gray there is in a color with less saturated colors, having a more gray component to them.
sentences.zh: 你也可以把饱和度理解为一个颜色里面含有多少灰色，饱和度较低的颜色含有更多的灰色成分。

sentences.en: And brightness is, you know, surprisingly enough, exactly what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 而明度，说实话，正如其听起来的那样。

sentences.en: It's really, you could think of it as how much white there is mixed into a color.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它理解为一个颜色里混合了多少白色。

sentences.en: So colors that are not very saturated, but are relatively bright, relax us.
sentences.zh: 因此，饱和度不高但明度相对较高的颜色会让我们放松。

sentences.en: So like a sage green that has lots of white mixed into it.
sentences.zh: 比如掺入了大量白色的鼠尾草绿。

sentences.en: So it's a light color.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一种浅色。

sentences.en: Well, we would find it relaxing to look at a color like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会觉得看着这样的颜色很放松。

sentences.en: Well, where a color, um, uh, that is more saturated, but not as bright, um, something like, uh, oh, I'll say a kelly green.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而某种颜色，嗯，嗯，饱和度更高但明度没那么高，嗯，类似于，嗯，哦，我可以说亮绿色。

sentences.en: Well, we find that, um, really, um, energizing to experience, but there are a couple, um, hues that have, uh, very particular, um, effects on us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会发现，嗯，真的，嗯，体验起来充满活力，但有几种，嗯，色相，嗯，对我们有非常特殊的，嗯，影响。

sentences.en: Like, um, seeing all sorts of different greens makes it more likely that we'll think creatively and, um, seeing reds, for example, um, degrades our analytical performance.
sentences.zh: 比如，嗯，看到各种不同的绿色会让我们更有可能进行创造性思考，而，嗯，看到红色，例如，嗯，会降低我们的分析表现。

sentences.en: Um, just for, just, just for starters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这只是，这只是，这只是开始。

sentences.en: And, um, there's a lot of other interesting research, um, that we can talk about.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，还有很多其他有趣的研究，嗯，我们可以讨论。

sentences.en: For example, um, when people are sitting on a, um, a, a cushion of some sort, um, you can think of that as like a haptic experience, a touch-based experience.
sentences.zh: 例如，嗯，当人们坐在，嗯，某种坐垫上时，嗯，你可以把这看作是一种触觉体验，一种基于触觉的体验。

sentences.en: Um, they are less likely to, um, drive as hard a bargain as when they're sitting on a harder surface.
sentences.zh: 嗯，与坐在较硬的表面上相比，他们不太可能，嗯，进行那么艰难的讨价还价。

sentences.en: Um, uh, when, um, we smell particular scents, um, even if they're very subtle and we've been being exposed to them for, and we've been exposed to them for a long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当，嗯，我们闻到特定的气味时，嗯，即使它们非常微妙，而且我们已经接触它们很长时间了，我们已经接触它们很长时间了。

sentences.en: Well, um, they have, um, significant influences on what goes on in our heads.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们，嗯，对我们脑海中发生的事情有着显著的影响。

sentences.en: Um, for example, when, um, uh, we smell lavender, we're more likely to trust, uh, those who are nearby and smelling, um, lemon is, um, likely to enhance our cognitive performance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，例如，当，嗯，我们闻到薰衣草味时，我们更有可能信任，嗯，附近的人，而闻到，嗯，柠檬味，嗯，可能会增强我们的认知表现。

sentences.en: So, you know, we can work our way through the senses one by one and see how various different, um, stimuli, um, influence how we think and behave.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们可以逐一探讨各种感官，看看各种不同的，嗯，刺激，嗯，是如何影响我们的思考和行为的。

sentences.en: And we can also think about more, uh, psychosocial type factors such as, um, you know, humans need for privacy, um, uh, uh, their need for control over their physical environment.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以考虑更多，嗯，心理社会类型的因素，例如，嗯，你知道的，人类对隐私的需求，嗯，嗯，嗯，他们对物理环境的控制需求。

sentences.en: Um, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，

sentences.en: basically everything you can see, hear, feel, et cetera, around you has some influence on what goes on in your brain.
sentences.zh: 基本上你周围能看到、听到、感受到的一切，等等，都会对你大脑中发生的事情产生一定的影响。

sentences.en: What about patterns?
sentences.zh: 那图案呢？

sentences.en: Are there any particular patterns that are more, maybe jarring or upsetting than other patterns or more soothing?
sentences.zh: 有没有哪些特定的图案比其他图案更让人觉得刺耳、不安，或者更让人舒缓？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting to think about patterns, um, because, you know, they're composed of different shapes and colors and types of lines and things like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，思考图案很有意思，嗯，因为，你知道的，它们由不同的形状、颜色、线条类型等组成。

sentences.en: And something that's, um, uh, really significant to consider when you're, um, choosing a pattern for a place in your life is the relative number of curving lines versus the
sentences.zh: 当你为生活中的某个地方选择图案时，有一个，嗯，非常重要的，嗯，需要考虑的因素是曲线的数量与

sentences.zh: 直线数量的相对比例，你知道的，而且，而且没有任何图案或地方是完全由曲线组成的。

sentences.en: I mean, that seems like a cartoon or entirely rectilinear, you know, a place that's all rectilinear makes you,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那看起来像卡通片，或者完全由直线组成，你知道的，一个全都是直线的地方让你，

sentences.en: well, that, that, that's like, um, an awful spaceship horror movie type interior.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那，那，那就像，嗯，糟糕的太空恐怖电影里的那种室内布景。

sentences.en: So when we're exposed to relatively more curvy lines, we, um, think a space is, um, more comfortable where,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们接触到相对更多的曲线时，我们，嗯，会认为一个空间，嗯，更舒适，而

sentences.en: when we're seeing mainly rectilinear lines, you know, straight lines, meaning at right angles, for example, well, thoughts of efficiency come to mind.
sentences.zh: 当我们主要看到直线时，你知道的，直线，比如以直角相交，嗯，就会让人联想到效率。

sentences.en: So, you know, these sorts of lines along with color, et cetera, are important considerations when patterns are being selected.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这些线条连同颜色等，在选择图案时都是重要的考虑因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's so fascinating that this is all happening really without us being cognizant of it.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了，这一切发生时我们甚至都没有意识到。

sentences.en: I think for the most part, um, and lighting too, I mean, for example, like I like to don't really like fluorescent lighting and I use a lamp in my office.
sentences.zh: 我想在大多数情况下，嗯，还有光线也是，我的意思是，例如，我不怎么喜欢荧光灯，我在办公室里用的是台灯。

sentences.en: So lighting is an important component to me.
sentences.zh: 所以光线对我来说是一个重要的组成部分。

sentences.en: Can you talk about the, you know, what it means to other people and what lighting is beneficial, what lighting is difficult for people?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈，你知道的，光线对其他人意味着什么，什么样的光线是有益的，什么样的光线对人们来说是困难的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.

sentences.en: When we're thinking about lighting, um, it's really important to align with whatever
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑光线时，嗯，非常重要的一点是，要与人们试图完成的事情，

sentences.en: out well, you know, and this should, would be no surprise to people because, you know, what do we do when we want to relax and hang out with people and have a good time?

sentences.en: in the middle of a table that people can gracefully divert, uh, divert their gaze to, um, when they need an eye contact break from others.
